findings.text: Per-CPU multiplexer state holds two independent atomic words per CPU, one for the currently enabled virtual interrupts and one for pending arrivals, reached through a per-CPU pointer plus a shared domain pointer and a callback that raises the underlying physical interrupt on a chosen CPU.

Masking clears the bit that corresponds to the descriptor hardware number in the local enable word. Unmasking sets that bit, orders the update against later reads, then re-checks the pending word and immediately requests a parent interrupt on the same CPU when the just-enabled bit was already pending, closing a race with concurrent senders.

Sending to a mask visits each target CPU, atomically records the virtual interrupt as pending with release ordering, orders that store before later reads, and issues a physical interrupt only when this sender newly set the bit and the target currently enables it, so redundant kicks are suppressed and prior shared-memory writes are visible to the receiver.

The multiplexer presents a single named interrupt chip offering mask, unmask and mask-send operations, and its domain allocator assigns consecutive virtual interrupts as per-CPU device interrupts, binding hardware number equal to allocation index to that chip with the per-CPU device handler; domain operations pair this allocator with the generic top-level free helper.

The receive entry reads the local enable word without extra ordering when invoked from interrupt context, atomically clears exactly the enabled pending bits, intersects the result with the enable snapshot, and dispatches each surviving hardware number through the shared multiplexer domain.

Creation is singleton and capacity-checked against the width of a plain integer word and a non-null send callback. It allocates per-CPU state, a named firmware node, a linear domain of the requested size, then tags the domain as single-IPI with IPI bus type and allocates its interrupts, storing domain and callback on success and unwinding domain, node and per-CPU storage in reverse order on failure.

Public inter-processor interrupt services comprise reservation and destruction of IPI ranges, lookup of the hardware number for a CPU, and single-target plus mask-target sends in checked and unchecked variants, all operating on virtual interrupt numbers and CPU masks.

Reservation rejects non-IPI or missing domains, destinations outside the possible set, and empty destinations. Single-hardware domains need one descriptor with zero offset regardless of holes, while per-CPU domains require a consecutive destination range and record the first CPU as offset. It allocates descriptors then hardware interrupts, freeing descriptors on hardware failure, and on success installs destination affinity, offset and a no-balancing mark on each descriptor.

Destruction validates descriptor, domain type and subset relationship to the original affinity, then frees one interrupt for shared-hardware domains or a weight-sized range adjusted by offset for per-CPU domains. Hardware lookup returns an invalid sentinel when data is missing, CPU out of range or outside affinity, selecting per-CPU data when needed. Send verification requires a capable chip, in-range CPU, present affinity and destination subset or membership.

Checked send entry points resolve descriptor, data and chip from the virtual number, warn once on verification failure, then delegate to unchecked variants. Unchecked paths verify only under debugging, prefer the native mask operation when present, otherwise loop over targets invoking single-target delivery, substituting the per-CPU descriptor for per-CPU domains and emulating missing single delivery with a singleton mask.

Interrupt allocation proceeds from descriptor allocation through parent chain allocation, hierarchical allocation, per-interrupt hierarchy trimming and mapping insertion, with reverse unwinding of hierarchy, chain and descriptors on any failure. A fixed base is reused when reallocating, otherwise descriptors are freshly allocated, and allocation helpers enforce presence of an allocator operation.

Release marks each descriptor non-requestable, detaches chip and handler, synchronizes the line and orders with a barrier, then walks each hierarchy level decrementing mapping counts and clearing reverse mappings before invoking hierarchical free, chain release and descriptor release, holding the root mutex only across mapping removal and hierarchical free.

Hierarchy allocation and bulk free serialize on the root domain mutex, bus-token updates serialize on a global domain mutex while rebuilding names and debug directories, reverse-map clearing asserts root mutex held, and nomap domains skip reverse-map maintenance entirely.

Chain construction embeds the outermost node in the descriptor and allocates one node per ancestor with shared common state, while insertion walks toward parents incrementing counts and installing hardware-to-data links and clearing the non-requestable mark. Trimming demands a valid outer chip, forbids valid chips beyond a single not-connected marker and empty chips before it, and severs plus frees the inner hierarchy when such a marker is present.

Domain delivery resolves a hardware number to a descriptor through the domain and then handles it, rejecting missing descriptors and rejecting enforced-context handlers invoked outside hard interrupt context before delegating to the generic descriptor handler.

Per-CPU device marking fails when the descriptor is missing or already marked and reports allocation failure distinctly. Descriptor allocation honors an explicit base or derives a non-zero hint from hardware number modulo total interrupt count with a retry from one. Total count comes from a global variable. Bus-token changes rebuild the domain name with the token and refresh its debug directory, tracking owned names. Firmware node release ignores null or foreign nodes and frees name plus container.

An alternate locked-allocation variant unconditionally rejects with an invalid argument, so availability depends on build configuration and callers must handle that failure. Creation rejects second instantiation and oversized requests, per-CPU reservation rejects gapped masks, and enforced-context handling is unsafe outside hard interrupt context.

Stable names are IPI Mux for the chip, IPI-Mux for the firmware node, and a genirq IPI log prefix; domain uses single-IPI flag with IPI bus token; descriptors use no-balancing on reservation and non-requestable during transitions; invalid hardware sentinel signals lookup failure; not-connected marks hierarchy trim; errors use invalid argument, no memory, busy and missing operation.
